ak_beer_climbs_2.blurb: A small cluster of five frozen routes on the lower slopes of Pioneer Peak, a short drive from Anchorage in the Knik River area. The grades run from easy water ice up to WI5, with a pair at WI3 and one at WI4, so it suits climbers stepping up from top-rope to leading as well as those after something steeper. Walk-ins are brief. Some lines finish on ledges with fixed anchors, and an easy descent is possible by lowering or rappelling. Because the cliff is low in elevation, the ice depends on cold stretches, and it makes a handy half-day outing.

ak_1st_fin.blurb: The lowest of the rock fins at Jaw Point, a coastal climbing area south of Juneau, and the one nearest the water. Expect a short climb uphill from the shoreline to reach it. The fin holds a small mix: an easy trad line only about 20 ft long that serves as a shortcut to a ledge, two sport routes of roughly 25 m both in the 5.12 range, and a pair of hard boulder problems around V5 to V6. It is more a spot for strong sport climbers and boulderers than for beginners, with one gentle scramble-style trad option.
